# Grouped bubble graph {#sec-grouped-bubble-charts}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
# fonts ----
library(extrafont)
library(sysfonts)
source("_common.R")
# use font
showtext::showtext_auto()
# set theme
ggplot2::theme_set(fmggp2::theme_powerrangers(
    base_size = 14))
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" appearance="simple"}
## Theme: `theme_powerrangers()`

Graphs in this chapter use `fmggp2::theme_powerrangers()`, built from the Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: a light gray background, a lightning gold frame, a red Copperplate title, and red, blue, yellow, pink, black, and green Ranger marks.
:::

:::: {.callout-note collapse="false" icon=false}

<br>

```{r}
#| label: full_code_display
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '60%'
#| out-width: '60%'
#| fig-align: right
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
set.seed(1993)
ranger_fights <- expand_grid(
  ranger = c("Red", "Blue", "Yellow", "Pink", "Black"),
  fight = 1:24) |>
  mutate(
    ranger = factor(ranger,
      levels = c("Red", "Blue", "Yellow", "Pink", "Black")),
    putty_rate = c(Red = 2.0, Blue = 1.2, Yellow = 1.6,
                   Pink = 1.4, Black = 1.8)[as.character(ranger)],
    fight_minutes = round(rgamma(n(), shape = 4, rate = 1), 1),
    putties_defeated = rpois(n(), lambda = putty_rate * fight_minutes),
    hits_taken = rpois(n(), lambda = 0.6 * fight_minutes))
labs_grp_bubble <- labs(
  title = "Power Rangers vs. the Putties",
  subtitle = "Putties defeated by fight length",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  x = "Fight length (minutes)",
  y = "Putties defeated",
  size = "Hits taken",
  fill = "Ranger")

ggp2_grp_bubble <- ranger_fights |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = fight_minutes, y = putties_defeated)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(size = hits_taken, fill = ranger),
        alpha = 2/3, shape = 21, color = "#000000") +
  scale_size(range = c(.04, 6))

ggp2_grp_bubble +
  labs_grp_bubble
```

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #02577A;"}
**Requirements:**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ a categorical variable**
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.05em; color: #282b2d;"}
**✅ two numeric (continuous) variables**
:::

::::

## Description

Grouped bubble graphs use position, color, and size to display the relationships between four variables (three numerical/quantitative, one categorical).

The position on the x and y axis captures the relationship between two numerical variables. The size and color of the points display a third numerical variable across the levels of a (fourth) categorical variable.

## Set up

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**PACKAGES:**
:::

Install packages.


::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: pkg_code_grp_bubble
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| results: hide
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr) # for data manipulation
library(tidyr) # for expand_grid()
```
:::


::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DATA:**
:::

Every episode of *Mighty Morphin Power Rangers* had the same rhythm: Rita Repulsa sent down a squad of Putties, and the Rangers kicked their way through them. We'll simulate 24 fights for each of the five original Rangers with four variables:

  - `fight_minutes`: how long the fight lasted, drawn from a gamma distribution with `rgamma()`

  - `putties_defeated`: a count from `rpois()`. Each Ranger has their own `putty_rate` (putties per minute), and the longer the fight, the more putties they defeat

  - `hits_taken`: another `rpois()` count, at 0.6 hits per minute for every Ranger

  - `ranger`: the Ranger, ordered red, blue, yellow, pink, and black so the theme colors match the suits

Setting the seed with `set.seed()` means you'll get the same 120 fights every time you run the code below.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: data_code_grp_bubble
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
set.seed(1993) # same 120 fights every time the code runs
ranger_fights <- expand_grid(
  ranger = c("Red", "Blue", "Yellow", "Pink", "Black"), # five Rangers
  fight = 1:24 # 24 fights for each Ranger
  ) |>
  mutate(
    ranger = factor(ranger,
      levels = c("Red", "Blue", "Yellow", "Pink", "Black")), # keep the order above
    putty_rate = c(Red = 2.0, Blue = 1.2, Yellow = 1.6, # Putties defeated per minute
                   Pink = 1.4, Black = 1.8)[as.character(ranger)], # (looked up for each Ranger)
    fight_minutes = round(rgamma(n(), shape = 4, rate = 1), 1), # fights last about 4 minutes
    putties_defeated = rpois(n(), lambda = putty_rate * fight_minutes), # longer fights, more Putties
    hits_taken = rpois(n(), lambda = 0.6 * fight_minutes) # longer fights, more hits
    )
glimpse(ranger_fights)
```
:::

## Distribution

In this grouped bubble chart, the `y` variable is a count that piles up over time. Longer fights don't just give more putties on average; they also give a wider range of possible counts, so each Ranger's points fan out as they move to the right. Below we'll move from the fights, to a picture, to the formula.

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**COUNT IT:**
:::

Start with the Red Ranger's first five fights.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_values_grp_bubble
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
ranger_fights |>
  filter(ranger == "Red") |>
  select(fight, fight_minutes, putties_defeated, hits_taken) |>
  head(5)
```
:::

Below we divide each Ranger's total putties by their total fight minutes to estimate their rate (`putties_per_min`), and compare it to the rate we built in (`putty_rate`).

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: count_summary_grp_bubble
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
ranger_rates <- ranger_fights |>
  group_by(ranger) |>
  summarise(putty_rate = first(putty_rate),
            putties_per_min = sum(putties_defeated) / sum(fight_minutes),
            hits_per_min = sum(hits_taken) / sum(fight_minutes))
ranger_rates
```
:::

Every putty estimate lands within a few tenths of the rate we built in. The hits per minute range from about `r round(min(ranger_rates$hits_per_min), 1)` to `r round(max(ranger_rates$hits_per_min), 1)` around the true rate of 0.6 (hits are rarer than putties, so their estimates bounce around more).

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**DRAW IT:**
:::

The graph below shows the Red and Blue Rangers' fights. Each line is the putty rate times the fight length, and each ribbon covers two standard deviations above and below the line. Both ribbons get wider as the fights get longer.

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: draw_grp_bubble
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
red_blue <- ranger_fights |>
  filter(ranger %in% c("Red", "Blue"))
ggplot(red_blue, aes(x = fight_minutes, fill = ranger, color = ranger)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(0, putty_rate * fight_minutes -
                                2 * sqrt(putty_rate * fight_minutes)),
                  ymax = putty_rate * fight_minutes +
                    2 * sqrt(putty_rate * fight_minutes)),
              alpha = 1 / 5, color = NA) +
  geom_line(aes(y = putty_rate * fight_minutes), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(aes(y = putties_defeated), size = 2) +
  labs(x = "Fight length (minutes)", y = "Putties defeated",
       color = "Ranger", fill = "Ranger")
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.10em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**NAME IT:**
:::

The putties in each fight follow a [Poisson distribution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poisson_distribution) whose average is the Ranger's rate ($\lambda$) times the length of the fight ($t$):

$$
\text{putties} \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda_{\text{ranger}} \times t)
$$

A Poisson count has a variance equal to its mean, so its standard deviation is $\sqrt{\lambda t}$. For the Red Ranger ($\lambda = 2$), a 2 minute fight averages 4 putties give or take about 2, while an 8 minute fight averages 16 putties give or take about 4. The spread grows with the square root of the fight length, which is why the points fan out (and why the ribbons in **DRAW IT** get wider). The `hits_taken` that set the bubble sizes work the same way with $\lambda = 0.6$, so bigger bubbles show up in longer fights for every Ranger. Try changing `rate = 1` to `rate = 4` in `rgamma()` and the fights get shorter, the points crowd to the left, and the fan almost disappears.

## Grammar


::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**CODE:**
:::

  - Create labels with `labs()`

  - Initialize the graph with `ggplot()` and provide `data`

  - Map `fight_minutes` to the `x` axis and `putties_defeated` to the `y` axis

  - Inside `geom_point()`

    - map `hits_taken` to `size` and `ranger` to `color`

    - set the `alpha` to `2/3`

  - In the `scale_size()`

    - set `range` to `c(.04, 6)`


::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_grp_bubble
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
labs_grp_bubble <- labs(
  title = "Power Rangers vs. the Putties",
  subtitle = "Putties defeated by fight length",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  x = "Fight length (minutes)",
  y = "Putties defeated",
  size = "Hits taken",
  color = "Ranger",
  fill = "Ranger")

ggp2_grp_bubble <- ranger_fights |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = fight_minutes, y = putties_defeated)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(size = hits_taken,
        color = ranger),
            alpha = 2/3) +
  scale_size(range = c(.04, 6))

ggp2_grp_bubble +
  labs_grp_bubble
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 1.15em; color: #1e83c8;"}
**GRAPH:**
:::

```{r}
#| label: create_graph_grp_bubble
#| eval: true
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| out-height: '100%'
#| out-width: '100%'
#| layout-nrow: 1
labs_grp_bubble <- labs(
  title = "Power Rangers vs. the Putties",
  subtitle = "Putties defeated by fight length",
  caption = "Simulated data",
  x = "Fight length (minutes)",
  y = "Putties defeated",
  size = "Hits taken",
  color = "Ranger",
  fill = "Ranger")

ggp2_grp_bubble <- ranger_fights |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = fight_minutes, y = putties_defeated)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(size = hits_taken,
        color = ranger),
            alpha = 2/3) +
  scale_size(range = c(.04, 6))

ggp2_grp_bubble +
  labs_grp_bubble
```

## More info

We can change the `shape` of the points for more control of the `color` and `fill`.

### Shape

Inside `geom_point()`, we can set `shape` to `21`, and `color` to `"#000000"` to outline the points in black

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_grp_bubble_s21
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
ggp2_grp_bubble_s21 <- ranger_fights |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = fight_minutes, y = putties_defeated)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(size = hits_taken, fill = ranger),
        alpha = 2/3, shape = 21, color = "#000000") +
  scale_size(range = c(.04, 6))

ggp2_grp_bubble_s21 +
  labs_grp_bubble
```
:::

### Color


Inside the `aes()` of `geom_point()`, we can set `shape` to `21`, and map `color` to `ranger` to outline the points in the same colors as `fill`

::: {style="font-size: 0.85em;"}
```{r}
#| label: code_graph_grp_bubble_s21_color
#| code-fold: show
#| eval: true
#| echo: true
ggp2_grp_bubble_s21_color <- ranger_fights |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = fight_minutes, y = putties_defeated)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(size = hits_taken,
        fill = ranger,
        color = ranger),
        alpha = 2/3, shape = 21) +
  scale_size(range = c(.04, 6))

ggp2_grp_bubble_s21_color +
  labs_grp_bubble
```
:::
